title: An accept deletes the merged branch even when it is ahead of its pushed copy
name: accept-branch-delete
description: Seen on 2026-09-24 in backup-attend-osc2. `deleteBranch` in packages/core/src/merge.ts:67 runs `git branch -d`. When a branch has an upstream, `-d` checks that the branch is merged into that upstream, not into HEAD. A node branch that was pushed for its draft PR and then got local commits (a merge from the base, a fix-up) is merged into the base but is ahead of `origin/sober/<node>`. So `-d` refuses, the `accept` tool returns `git branch -d … failed`, and the merge, the worktree removal and the done mark have already happened. The user sees an error for an accept that succeeded. Fix: after the merge, check `git merge-base --is-ancestor <branch> HEAD` and then delete with `-D`. Only a branch that is not in HEAD is refused, with a clear sentence. Test in packages/core/src/merge.test.ts (or the file that holds the accept tests): a branch with an upstream it is ahead of, merged into the base, is deleted with no error.
